items.summary: The US Department of Justice said on 12 November 2026 that a court has authorised the seizure or freezing of more than 1.2 billion US dollars in cryptocurrency stolen from Binance. More than 2.7 billion dollars have already been frozen. The FBI attributes the theft to the North Korean group it calls TraderTraitor. The same DOJ release also covers a separate scheme, FaceStealer, in which fake video meetings were used to steal more than 400 million dollars over 18 months; that is not a new Binance theft.

items.summary: Norwegian Block Exchange (NBX) and Aprikos Venture have signed a joint venture for a planned Pakistan crypto exchange, Nayapaisa, and have applied to the Pakistan Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority for a No Objection Certificate, according to the companies as reported by Kaupr. The application is the first step in a licensing process, and the exchange will not serve customers until both the certificate and a licence are granted. The plan is to offer deposits and withdrawals in Pakistani rupees through licensed Pakistani banks.

items.summary: Binance co-founder and co-chief executive Yi He said Kaiser Ng is leaving as chief financial officer after more than five years to pursue a new venture, with a transition plan that has been under way for about six months, according to The Block and The Globe and Mail. Justin Yek, previously vice-president of finance at Airwallex, is taking over as CFO. The announcement came days after the late-October theft from Binance; Yi He did not say the departure was caused by the incident.

items.summary: The Norwegian crypto exchange Firi recorded 19.8 million kroner in crypto trading the day after the Binance hack — more than double a typical day — according to figures Firi shared with E24. Activity stayed high over the weekend at 15.4 million kroner, 50 percent above the next-busiest weekend so far this year, chief executive Thuc Hoang told E24. Hoang says it is too early to know whether customers are permanently moving funds from foreign exchanges.

items.summary: According to a Binance post on X on 3 November, the attackers behind the recent theft approached an engineer in September with a fake job interview and got him to download a "task" containing malware. Binance says the attackers then used his laptop and misused an internal AI tool to take over the computers of two other engineers. DR reports that Binance has covered 98 percent of the losses; on 31 October Binance said about 90 percent had been replaced.

items.summary: North Korea has rejected the FBI's statement that North Korean hackers were behind the theft from Binance, calling it an 'absurd fabrication' in a statement by Kim Yo-jong carried by the state news agency KCNA, according to Yonhap and Bloomberg. The statement calls the attribution a political provocation and suggests it could affect dialogue between North Korea and the United States. The FBI said on 31 October that North Korea's TraderTraitor was responsible and published addresses linked to the stolen funds; the denial is North Korea's position, not a new finding.

items.summary: According to Binance, customers withdrew a net of about 3.64 billion US dollars between 07:00 and 16:30 CET on 1 November 2026, after the exchange reopened withdrawals following the hack: about 4.65 billion went out and 1.01 billion came in. Binance says this equals about 2.1 percent of its 171 billion dollars in assets and that withdrawals are levelling off. According to CNBC, the stablecoin issuer Circle has now frozen more than 1.1 billion USDC. The analytics service DefiLlama reports higher outflow figures, which Binance disputes because they do not account for its own transfers to new wallets.

items.summary: Binance began reopening withdrawals in stages from 07:00 CET on 1 November 2026, and by 13:36 CET all 15 networks in the first phase were open, including Bitcoin, Ethereum, BNB Smart Chain and Solana, according to the exchange. Binance says withdrawals now go out from new wallet addresses and that its Proof of Reserves address list has been updated. The exchange also says that 6 billion US dollars of the loss from the 29 October hack has been covered.

items.summary: The FBI said on 31 October 2026 that North Korea was responsible for the theft of more than 6 billion US dollars in crypto assets from Binance on or about 29 October, and named the activity 'TraderTraitor', which is linked to the Lazarus group. The blockchain analytics firms TRM Labs and Chainalysis had already linked the attack to the same group. According to the FBI, the stolen assets are mainly being converted into Ether, and the FBI, the US Secret Service and IRS-CI are asking crypto service providers to block transactions with the listed addresses.

items.summary: Binance confirms that it lost about 6.3 billion US dollars in the security incident on 29 October 2026, and says about 3 billion of that has been frozen. According to Binance, deposits are working normally and withdrawals are expected to reopen within 48 hours. The exchange says its investigation has found additional points of breach beyond the compromised employee computer identified earlier, and that user losses will be covered from its SAFU emergency fund and its own funds.
